items.title: Hypolite Charles Interview, 1963-04-13
items.q: The same fellow you see I got in that picture there, he played saxophone also.

ctx.x: yeah, that's right, because we used to use clarinet. And then the clarinet player took it. Then they double up on second clarinet. But the clarinet was the main one. All those bands was using when I went into the city of New Orleans, from 19, I'm sure from 1909 up until 1916, that's all they were using, clarinet. Then they began to use saxophone, because I've used saxophone myself. The same fellow you see I got in that picture there, he played saxophone also.
You mean Sam Dutry? Sam Dutry.

Did the musicians, I had already asked if you used any Cajun folk songs from this area, you said no. Were there any musicians from Latin America, you know, South America, that came in there that at any time that your group heard play or that played with you, that would give you any, say, Latin rhythms? Do you recall any kind of music of this kind being used?
